children: -Soybeans for November delivery rose 2.4% to $13.18 1/2 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade on Tuesday, on hopes that the Environmental Protection Agency will approve smaller small-refinery waivers for biofuels blending in 2026 and 2027.
-Corn for December delivery rose 1.4% to $5.45 1/2 a bushel.
-Wheat for December delivery rose 0.9% to 7.81 a bushel.

Demand Math: Soybean futures breached $13 a bushel for the first time since December 2023 on news of the EPA's revision to 2025 biofuel-blending exemption rules. The agency says that 1.76 billion in Renewable Identification Numbers are being exempted for small refineries in 2025, which is more than expected by the market, and traders are looking at the future impact. "They are expected to be re-allocated to 2026 and 2027, so the news was actually viewed as a little supportive as a smaller amount of exemptions was expected to be allowed," said Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives in a note.

Looking for the Knockout: Russia and Ukraine's conflict is increasingly focused on either side disrupting the flow of commodity shipments from the other. CBOT wheat prices move higher as two of the world's leading wheat exporters squeeze the global supply. "Both Ukraine and Russia appear to believe that the attacks on commodity logistics provides them an edge in bringing their opponent to their knees economically," said Arlan Suderman of StoneX in a note. "As such, the war on commodity logistics continues in both regions, threatening both energy and food commodity movement out of two commodity-rich regions of the world."

Brighter Future: CBOT futures jumped to their highest levels in years, giving farmers a new optimism about their future prospects. The Purdue University-CME Group Ag Economy Barometer Index increased to 135 points in August from 126 points in July, which the group attributes mostly to an improvement among farmers to their future expectations. "For the first time since June 2025, a higher proportion of respondents expect their operation to be better off financially than worse off a year from now," said the group in a press release.

Weather Threat: A "super" El Niño climate system this winter is expected to elevate agricultural commodity prices in the southern hemisphere. In a research note, Arkady Gevorkyan of Citi Research said that sugar futures have the most near-term upside, potentially climbing to 22 cents a pound over the next 12 months on excessive rainfall. Wheat in Argentina is also expected to receive large amounts of rain.

Modern Solutions: The USDA is implementing changes to improve how it gathers and reports data on U.S. crop production. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said Tuesday that the department will team up with NASA to use satellite imagery and computerized models to create more accurate forecasts of how many bushels of crops farmers grow across the country. The plans are speculated to boost the number of farmers who take part in the department's surveys. "A push should and probably will be done to have farmers input survey responses on their computers and/or other devices," Ag Bull Trading analyst Jim Wiesemeyer said.
-The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.
-The Campbell's Co. will release its fourth quarterly earnings report at 7:15 a.m. ET Thursday.
-The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
